result.title: SIRAZ: Sparse Inter-Layer Residual Aggregation for Zero-Shot Visual Neural Decoding
result.summary: Brain-computer interfaces aim to establish direct communication between neural activity and external systems, making interpretation of brain signals an important problem. In this context, neural visual decoding seeks to infer visual information from neural activity by learning a mapping between brain responses and the corresponding visual stimuli. It investigates how visual information emerges from neural signals and relates to perceptual processing while enabling the reconstruction or retrieval of visual stimuli from neural signals. Our brain primarily follows a hierarchical pathway to process visual information captured by the eye. However, neural representations learned by existing methods differ fundamentally from those produced by the biological visual system. To bridge this gap and mimic the human vision hierarchy, we introduce Sparse Inter-layer Residual Aggregation for Zero-shot (SIRAZ). SIRAZ is a framework that aligns neural visual representations by jointly modeling early visual processes via fovea- and magnocellular-pathway-inspired Difference-of-Gaussians transformations. To align the semantic information with neural information, it extracts multiple intermediate representations of the image at multiple depths and passes them through the Residual Gated Adapter Mechanism. To study the temporal dynamics of neural signals, the Direction-aware Multi-Scale Temporal Attention Encoder is introduced to align the learned neural representation with the final visual representation. The proposed framework achieves 92.5% top-1 and 99.27% top-5 accuracy in the intra-subject setting on the THINGS-EEG dataset, and 50.25% and 75% top-1 and top-5 accuracy in the THINGS-MEG dataset. The results indicate that combining biologically motivated visual representations with the structured modalities of neural dynamics improves cross-modal alignment and zero-shot image retrieval.

AI.brief_summary: SIRAZ 面向零样本视觉神经解码，用模拟外周与早期视觉通路的 Difference-of-Gaussians 变换、多深度图像中间表示经残差门控适配器聚合，以及方向感知多尺度时间注意力编码 EEG/MEG 动态，以对齐神经与视觉表示并提升图像检索。
AI.relevance_reason: 任务本身是神经信号到图像的跨模态对齐而非 VLM 推理，但其稀疏跨层残差聚合与多深度特征门控选择，可能为 LVR 中多层视觉证据筛选与内部状态融合提供参照，需核查其聚合是否真保留细粒度视觉内容。
